evals.prompt: This is our own 8-second UGC clip: a guy on a couch drinks from a green energy-drink can, sets it down, and talks to camera. Swap the can for our approved Volt Zero packshot and keep everything else, including his voice.
evals.expected_output: A product swap package: the muted master as @Video 1 (an asset:// video, since the clip shows a person) with the source audio saved for an original-audio post route, the packshot as @Image 1 with background and lighting excluded, the five-part swap contract with per-cut count, contact windows for grip, drink and set-down, generate_audio false, edit task type, and a 480p contact-window probe as the first rung.
expectations: The original can is identified by observable descriptors (colour, which hand, first appearance), never as 'the product'.
The prompt states that the entire video contains exactly one target can and includes a Timeline Inheritance clause.
@Video 1 is the muted master, generate_audio is false, no @Audio binding is used, and the original-audio post route is stated for his voice.
Because the clip shows a person, the package recommends uploading the muted master to the Virtual Portrait library and binding @Video 1 as asset://.
Grip, mouth contact and set-down windows are listed with approximate times.
The first proposed block is a 480p probe, and the package is delivered in chat as a paste-ready block; the skill does not generate, upload or submit anything.

evals.prompt: Replace the woman on the right in this two-person cafe scene with our character Lia. Keep the man on the left untouched.
evals.expected_output: A single-character swap that recommends uploading Lia's approved views to the Virtual Portrait library and binds them as asset:// references, the right-hand woman identified by position, clothing and action, source accessories named so they do not carry over, and the man listed under preservation.
expectations: Lia's approved views are recommended for Virtual Portrait upload and bound as asset:// references by binding position, never by asset ID.
The replaced woman is identified by screen position, clothing and action, and the man on the left is explicitly preserved.
The prompt states exactly one Lia and that she wears only the wardrobe in her reference.
The swap is not routed to Motion Transfer, because only one person changes.
Before writing the prompt, the agent asks the user to confirm rights for the cafe footage and the people in it.

evals.prompt: Swap the product and also change the whole background to a beach and make everyone wear summer clothes.
evals.expected_output: A routing response: several element classes and most of the frame change, so the request is split into sequential swaps or routed to Motion Transfer, with the trade-off explained before any prompt is written.
expectations: The skill does not write one swap prompt that changes product, location and every outfit at once.
It proposes either sequential single-class swaps, with the user judging each result before the next, or a Motion Transfer recast, and explains the difference.
Nothing is generated or submitted.

evals.prompt: Swap the blue mug in our owned stop-motion clip for this approved orange mug. No people are visible. It is exactly 120 frames at 24 fps, with the set-down on the final frame. The selected edit destination supports this input. Preserve all timing and the saved audio; prompt only.
evals.expected_output: A single-object swap preserving the full five-second source span and final contact, without an empirical frame-count trim.
expectations: Preserves exact source timing and the final-frame set-down; does not change the input to 121 or 113 frames.
Uses the muted source and original-audio post route, with contact and timeline inheritance preserved.
Checks actual output timing rather than promising equal frame counts or accepting a blanket 0.3-second loss.

evals.prompt: The current destination documentation requires an 8n+1 frame input for my 120-frame owned product clip. I have not approved any timing change. Explain the next step without generating or modifying files.
evals.expected_output: A constraint-driven adaptation proposal that keeps the original untouched and asks for agreement.
expectations: Distinguishes this verified destination requirement from a universal frame-count rule.
Does not silently trim, pad or retime; explains the timing tradeoff and asks for agreement before making a separate copy.
Preserves the original video and audio and records any agreed adaptation; does not promise exact model output timing.
